description: A compatibility-preserving diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that measures the trained recommender’s behavior and constructs an interpretation prompt from measured metrics and their definitions. It supports architecture changes while retaining the native diagnostic interface and the shared RecHarness evaluation protocol.
motivation: Ground model revisions in reproducible diagnostics while preventing fabricated user attributes, unavailable metadata, and hidden-test leakage. Compare revisions using macro-average validation HR@10 across all four Amazon categories.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions. Probe the actual view.model and adapt feature extraction and scoring when the architecture changes. Batches contain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors shaped B x L. Use only public interaction histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; treat simulator diversity and conformity traits as unobserved. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category. Preserve dataset routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the pinned evaluator. Any architecture change must also update the predictor writer.
pseudocode:
probe = DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
raw = probe.run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)
assert raw contains metrics and metric_definitions
prompt = diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw)
interpret measured findings without inferring unavailable attributes
use findings to propose compatible model revisions
train and evaluate revisions under the fixed protocol
select using macro-average validation HR@10 across four categories

originality.positive: Connects model diagnostics to an iterative recommendation workflow through an explicit compatibility contract.
originality.negative: The description specifies an adapter and evaluation constraints rather than a new diagnostic algorithm or recommendation method.

future_potential.positive: Could support systematic comparisons across architectures and help identify useful model revisions.
future_potential.negative: Utility depends on the diagnostic metrics chosen and whether their interpretations predict validation improvements; no evidence is supplied.

code_difficulty.positive: Explicit interfaces and batch shapes make the adapter scope clear.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture-aware probes, full-catalog scoring, and consistent training and inference implementations require careful integration.
